problem.title: The Gram-square structure and the real structure of face space
problem.statement: Derive that the full three-family Yukawa form is the square of a face-space map; find, or refute, a real structure on the complexified face space under which the bracket form has signature $(1,2)$ on the physical slice; and account for the quarks' failure of the Koide relation, which the perturbative strong dressing cannot produce from Koide brackets.
problem.why: The Gaussian section and the alignment result assume the Gram-square form; the real structure would promote Koide's light-cone reading from a choice to a consequence; the quark account decides whether the relation is selective at bracket level at all.
problem.known: The alignment result rests on the Gram-square form (\claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(3)); the light-cone reading is a choice in \claimref{families.koide-nullity-condition-one-member-invariant}; the face identification is a working hypothesis (\claimref{families.hyp-face-identification}). Under the adopted premise of slot covariance (\claimref{families.slot-covariance-of-mass-law}), a family form sesquilinear in the face vector, with constant coefficients and face-wise diagonal $2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$, is forced to be the Gram square, exact at $\Lambda = 0$ and rank one, while the permutations alone leave a nine-dimensional freedom (\claimref{synthesis.slot-covariance-forces-gram-square}). The real structure is found: the one on which the bracket form is Lorentzian is complex conjugation conjugated by the doublet quarter-turn, under which the bracket form becomes the light-cone member, so the real structure and the choice of member are one datum and the physical vector is null on no slice; the Koide angle is the Hilbert-Schmidt angle between the mass matrix and the identity (\claimref{synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-turn}). Every $S_{3}$-equivariant real structure gives the same geometry with the coherent source after a face unitary (\claimref{synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-stabiliser-to-z2}(i)), so nothing built covariantly in face space can select the Lorentzian member. The Gaussian coherent face vector lies on no permutation-equivariant real slice, and its projection satisfies Koide exactly when the channel feeding ratio is $\lambda^{2} = 2$ (\claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}). The third part, the strong dressing, is answered in the negative at perturbative level: a dressing that is flavour-blind or favours the lighter quarks can only lower the Koide quotient, the measured quark quotients exceed $\tfrac23$ in both sectors at every standard mass definition (between $0.731$ and $0.889$), and perturbative QCD running, pole conversion and constituent dressing are of that kind (argued, standard QCD: \claimref{synthesis.imported-flavour-blind-quark-mass-running}, \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-pole-mass-relation}), so they cannot turn Koide brackets into the measured quark masses; a Koide bracket would need a dressing favouring the heaviest quark by at least $1.88$ (down) and $8.67$ (up, own-scale masses); dressings that raise the middle mass and lower the lightest relative to the heaviest are not treated (\claimref{synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide}). The selectivity observation is restated accordingly (\claimref{families.selectivity-observation-level}). Both parts of the success clause are met, the first under a premise, but the light-cone reading stays a choice rather than a consequence, and whether the quark brackets satisfy the relation at all is open. The one quark triple near the relation is a look-elsewhere effect: over the twenty quark triples at three mass definitions (sixty quotients spread from $0.448$ to $0.987$) the nearest to $\tfrac23$ is $(c, b, t)$ at own-scale masses, $0.6693$, against a nearest deviation of about $0.0045$ expected by chance, and it moves with the mass definition ($0.6575$ with the charm pole mass, $0.7209$ at $M_{Z}$); so the $(c, b, t)$ relation (Rodejohann and Zhang 2011, cited from memory) is no evidence that quark brackets satisfy Koide, while the lepton triple, a single triple within about $5 \times 10^{-6}$, is far from chance (computed with masses partly cited from memory, not filed).
attack: Decide whether the quark brackets satisfy the Koide relation at all: the dressing that would reconcile them must favour the heaviest quark, which no perturbative strong effect does; test the remaining class ($D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$) or drop the selectivity account for quarks. The $(c, b, t)$ near-hit is at chance level and does not count.

Look for what would make the light-cone member a consequence: since the real structure and the member are one datum (\claimref{synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-turn}) and every equivariant real structure looks the same from the source, the selection must come from structure outside face space.
problem.success: The Gram-square form derived from stated structure, and a real structure found or excluded.

entities.title: Koide as a nullity condition, for one member of the invariant family
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: The Koide relation is equivalent to the family vector being null for the equal-coefficient member $s^{2} - Q(d)$ of the $S_{3}$-invariant quadratic forms, a member that is chosen rather than forced.

entities.title: Selectivity, at observation level
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: Under Hypothesis (S) leptons are undressed colour singlets and quarks strongly dressed, but the known strong dressing can only lower the Koide quotient and the quarks are already above $\tfrac23$, so it does not explain the quarks' failure; seesaw-composed neutrinos are exempt; at observation level.

entities.title: Slot covariance of the family mass law: a flavour symmetry of the law, broken by the state
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: Premise: the family mass law is covariant under the slot mixing $U(3)$ of the three-spinor system, a flavour symmetry of the law broken by the state, which forces the rank-one Gram square.

entities.title: Slot covariance forces the Gram square
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: For a family form sesquilinear in the face vector $\beta$ with constant coefficients and face-wise diagonal $2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$, covariance under the three-spinor slot mixing $U(3)$ (under which $\beta$ transforms by the cofactor law), assumed as the premise of slot covariance, forces the Gram square $2\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}$ (exact at $\Lambda = 0$, rank one), while the permutations alone leave a nine-dimensional affine freedom including a face-wise form with three equal families.

entities.title: The Lorentzian Koide slice is a quarter-turn of the doublet
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: The face-space real structure on which the bracket form is Lorentzian is complex conjugation conjugated by the doublet quarter-turn $P_{s} + I_4 P_{d}$, under which the bracket form becomes the light-cone member, so it adds nothing to that choice and the physical vector is null on no slice; and the Gram-square property is automatic, the Koide angle selecting only the positive square root.

entities.title: The coherent face vector meets no real slice
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: The Gaussian coherent face vector lies on no permutation-equivariant real slice for any channel phase, every slice projection keeps half its doublet norm, and the projected vector satisfies Koide exactly when the channel feeding ratio is $\lambda^{2} = 2$, the choice of slice moving only the Koide phase by a quarter turn (up to orientation).

entities.title: Mass-ordered dressing cannot turn Koide brackets into quark masses
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: The Koide quotient is unchanged by a common dressing factor and strictly lowered by raising the lighter masses, so a strong dressing that is flavour-blind at a common scale and favours the lighter quarks at own scales, as pole masses or as constituent masses (argued from standard QCD) can only lower it; with the measured quark quotients above $\tfrac23$ in both sectors (between $0.731$ and $0.889$), a Koide bracket would need a dressing favouring the heaviest quark by at least $1.88$ (down) and $8.67$ (up).

entities.title: The real structure leaves a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ stabiliser and cannot give 207
entities.subject: generations
entities.one_liner: Every $S_{3}$-equivariant real structure and the coherent source $\kappa(u' + \lambda e^{I_4\chi}f_{+})$ are carried by a face unitary to conjugation and the line of $(1, a, I_4 a)$, $a = \lambda/\sqrt2$, with a phase independent of $\chi$; the residual symmetry is the single reflection $R_{n}$, $n = c_{R}\times c_{I}$ (at the Koide point the reflection of the Koide vector through the democratic axis), which forces $n$ to be an exact eigenvector of the face mass form (at the floor, so the lowest, in every state built from the source, its conjugate and $\hat{V}$, not in general) and leaves a five-parameter block that exact Fock instances fill, while a cubic family word has no residual symmetry at all: the $207$ cannot come from the real structure or the cubic family word acting by covariance, only from the selected state.
